items.headline: How I Blew Up My Business To Save My Life
items.angle: Christian shares a vulnerable story about hitting a breaking point with hustle culture, where his successful business was costing him his life. He then outlines his decision to rebuild it from the ground up using the principles that would become FieldWork.
hooks: My business was making 6 figures. It was also ruining my life.
It was a Tuesday in October. I shut my laptop and told my wife, 'I can't do this anymore.'
I had two choices: burn out completely, or burn the whole business down and start over.
The 'hustle culture' playbook almost cost me my family. Here's what I did instead.
For years, I believed success meant being 'always on.' I was completely wrong.
talking_points: My business was successful on paper, but it was costing me everything that mattered. My time, my health, my presence with my family.
I remember one specific moment, I was stuck on a client call, watching my son play outside through the office window. I realized I wasn't building a life, I was building a cage.
I had followed the standard advice. Grind it out, be available 24/7, trade every hour of my day for a dollar. I was a ghost in my own home.
Faced with that reality, I had two choices. I could keep going down that path and eventually lose the very family I was working so hard for.
Or, I could burn it all down. I could let go of the clients, the revenue, and the identity I had built, and start over with a new set of rules.
I chose to rebuild. I spent the next six months obsessively learning about automation, systems, and AI. I designed a new kind of business from the ground up.
The goal was simple: it had to run without me being chained to a desk. It had to be an engine for my life, not the center of it.
Today, that new business not only supports my family, but it gives me the freedom to actually live. To be present, to go on adventures, to get back into the field.
This is the exact philosophy and system I now teach inside my program, FieldWork. It's for people who want to build online so they can live offline.

Do not let the hustle narrative beat you down into a burnt out, always on, people pleaser. The world is loud, but you can build a calm, profitable business that serves you.

items.headline: The Founder's Glitch
items.angle: Instead of a technical glitch, frame the 'glitch' as the common but flawed founder mindset. It's the moment an entrepreneur realizes the business they built for freedom has become a digital prison, a bug in their life's operating system.
hooks: The Founder's Glitch.
The Hustle Hangover.
You built a calendar cage.
The expert's trap.
Your freedom business isn't.
talking_points: Let's talk about the Founder's Glitch.
It's that moment you look up from your laptop and realize the business you built to create freedom has actually just built you a more comfortable cage.
The symptoms are pretty common. You check Slack before you've had your coffee. Your family asks if you're listening, but you're a thousand miles away thinking about a client email.
You take a 'vacation' but it's just you answering messages from a slightly nicer chair with a better view.
This isn't a personal failing. It's a system glitch. You've been sold a version of success that requires your constant presence.
The fix isn't to work harder or to optimize your burnout.
The fix is to build intelligent systems, using AI and automation, that do the work for you.
You build the engine once, so you can get back to your life. So you can truly live offline.
This is the entire philosophy behind our program, FieldWork.
If you're feeling that glitch, comment the word 'SYSTEMS' below. I'll send you our free guide on the first three automations you can build to start buying your time back.

items.headline: The Automation vs. Hiring ROI
items.angle: Adapt the competitor's polarizing ROI framework to the world of online business. Contrast the common 'solution' of hiring more people with the FieldWork philosophy of building automated systems to create leverage and buy back time.
hooks: I firmly believe most founders get a greater ROI from building one great system than from hiring their next employee.
Here's a hard truth: Your time has a greater ROI spent building automated assets than it does servicing more clients.
I believe there is a greater return on investment in a business that funds your life than in a business that becomes your life.
Controversial opinion: The ROI on learning to build with AI is higher than the ROI on hiring another virtual assistant.
I firmly believe you get a better ROI from one month spent building systems than from six months spent chasing growth.
talking_points: I firmly believe that for most founders, there is a greater ROI in building one great automated system than in hiring their next employee.
I know that sounds backwards. We are taught that growth means growing your team.
But hiring another person just adds another layer of management, communication, and complexity to your day.
A new hire might save you ten hours a week, but you will spend five of those hours managing them.
A well built system, on the other hand, works for you 24/7. It does the job perfectly every single time without needing a coffee break.
Think about an automated client onboarding sequence versus manually emailing and scheduling with every new person. One is leverage, the other is a bottleneck.
This is not about replacing people. It is about using technology to handle the repetitive tasks so your team, and you, can focus on what matters.
It is how you build a business that serves your life, instead of a life that serves your business.
